newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares seen up, trade likely to be volatile.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares seen up, trade likely to be volatile.

text.p: Brazil shares are likely to keep rising Monday if investors continue to pump fresh money into the market, brokers said.
On Friday, the bolsa ended strong on a surprising hefty volume of over one billion reais, boosted by increased domestic and foreign buy orders.
But analysts noted volatility is expected to intensify in coming sessions ahead of next week's options and futures settlements.
The options will settle on June 16, while the futures index contracts will be liquidated two days later.
Congressional activity could also bolster market sentiment this week, analysts said.
Brokers expect lawmakers to vote on a general telecommunications law outlining rules for the privatization of the telecom sector and amendments to the administrative reform.

Also disqualified consortia for the closely watched Band B selloff are likely to appeal the Communications Ministry's decision this week. Last Wednesday, the ministry announced that five of 15 bidders were disqualified.
Blue-chip activity Friday:
Telebras up 2.23 pct at 146.70 reais
Eletrobras off 0.1 pct at 512 reais
Vale do Rio Doce up 0.4 pct at 23.10 reais
Petrobras up 4.44 pct at 249 reais Sao Paulo stock exchange's Bovespa index of the 48 most-traded shares:
* Friday: up 2.05 percent at 11,334 points
* Week: flat
* Month: flat
* Year-to-date: up 60.9 pct
Hot stocks: Banking stocks could continue climbing on speculation about eventual mergers and acquisitions.

Sao Paulo state bank Banespa shares may also post further gains on privatization prospects. The bank's preferred share has risen over 70 percent since the bank was transferred to federal hands in a prior step to its selloff.
SELIC (open): 2.30 pct
Dollar/Real (open): 1.0730 per dollar
